purpose: Edoxaban is used to lower the risk of stroke and dangerous blood clots in people who have an irregular heartbeat called atrial fibrillation. It is also used to treat blood clots in the legs (deep vein thrombosis) and lungs (pulmonary embolism), and to prevent them from coming back.
how_it_works: Your blood naturally forms clots to stop bleeding, but sometimes clots can form in the wrong places and cause serious problems like a stroke. Edoxaban works by blocking a specific protein in your blood called Factor Xa, which is needed to make clots. By blocking this protein, the medicine helps keep your blood flowing smoothly and reduces the chance of harmful clots forming.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is bleeding, which can show up as bruising more easily than usual, bleeding that takes longer to stop, nosebleeds, or bleeding gums. You may also notice blood in your urine (pink or red color) or darker stools. Some people experience mild rash or anemia.
warnings: This medicine increases your risk of bleeding, so let your doctor or pharmacist know before any surgery, dental work, or procedure. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can increase your stroke risk. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, since many can interact with edoxaban. If you notice unusual or heavy bleeding, severe headache, dizziness, or coughing up blood, seek medical help right away.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for most adults is 60 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. If you have kidney problems, weigh less than 60 kg (about 132 lbs), or take certain other medicines, your doctor may lower your dose to 30 mg once a day. Always take it at the same time each day and never skip or double up on doses.
